title.narrative: Output 2.4. Increased capacity Member States to apply sectoral international labour standards, codes of practice and guidelines

description.narrative:
A Regional workshop on Investing in Early Childhood Care and Education in the Arab Region for a More Gender Equal World of Work was held in Amman, Jordan, 15-16 May 2023. The workshop brought together over 90 participants from 13 countries in the region. The workshop adopted action plans for seven countries/territories in the region (Bahrain, Egypt, Jordan, Lebanon, OPT, Saudi Arabia, and Yemen) as well as thematic recommendations for the region.
Following the workshop, in Jordan the Office has worked with the Technical and Vocational Skills Development Commission on job profiles and a training manual for workers. A new collective bargaining agreement was signed which brings new labour rights to workers in private nurseries, kindergartens and schools, including caregivers and teachers. In Palestine, a study was launched to establish a cooperative for childcare. For other countries, the Office is following up on implementation later in the year. With the support from Norway and the Swedish International Development Agency and in collaboration with UN Women, the ILO supported in the coordination of the efforts among stakeholders and the organization of a regional conference that facilitated the adoption of the Framework. The ILO facilitated the drafting of action plans for countries in the Arab States plus Palestine and followed up with each to support plans implementation.

description.narrative: The Ministry of Agriculture has implemented an initiative to promote decent work in rural areas through the afforestation of approximately in 1,750 dunums (175 Ha) by planting 90,000 forest trees in the governorates of Irbid and Jerash, in Jordan. This initiative plays a crucial role in supporting the National Afforestation Plan that creates green jobs in rural areas for both Jordanians and Syrians, with a focus on youth. As water scarcity is a major barrier to Irbid’s and Jerash’s development, the initiative relies on a green innovative cocoon technology, leading to a 90 percent reduction in water consumption for irrigation. The implementation of this initiative is contributing to advance decent work and a just transition in the rural economy by promoting green jobs and rural skills, enhancing the sustainable management of natural resources, and improving rural livelihoods. All these elements are pivotal to combat the climate crisis. The ILO, with support of the Government of Germany through the KFW Development Bank, has entered into an agreement with the Ministry of Agriculture. This agreement emphasizes the importance of creating green decent paid employment opportunities in rural areas, building on the longstanding Employment-Intensive Investment Programme (EIIP) experience in Jordan. Under this agreement, through the ILO employment intensive approach, this initiative is expected to result in the creation of 110,000 person days of paid decent employment for 1,250 individuals (50% Jordanian, 50% Syrian, 30 % Women and 5% people with disabilities) and members of host communities residing in rural areas, while providing them with suitable skills that will help them to get job opportunities in the future.
